title: The unramified parameter open for a closed locally finite type source
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$ and $f:A\to C$ be morphisms with $q\circ f=p$, and assume that $p$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and is a closed map on underlying spaces (images of closed subsets are closed). Then $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $U_f\subseteq A$ be the union of the open subschemes on which $f$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. The subset $B_0=|B|\setminus p(|A|\setminus |U_f|)$ is open and has its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to B$, the induced morphism $f_T:A\times_BT\to C\times_BT$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is unramified if and only if $h$ factors through $B_0\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tag 05X8, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-unramified, scheme specialization; original item steps 1--4 (finite-type cancellation, point lifting, unramified locus and closed-image complement).

proof.text: Apply clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to the triangle $A\xrightarrow{f}C\xrightarrow{q}B$. Its composite is $p$, which is locally of finite type by hypothesis, so $f$ is locally of finite type. This uses no finiteness or separatedness hypothesis on $q$.

Apply [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change] to $f$. Its open $W_f$ is exactly the union $U_f$ in the statement. Put $Z=|A|\setminus |U_f|$. This is closed; since $p$ is a closed map, $p(Z)$ is closed in $|B|$, and its complement $B_0$ is open. Equip it with the open subscheme structure: restrict $\mathcal O_B$ to this open, which is locally covered by open affine charts of $B$. Its inclusion is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 05X8, lemma-where-unramified, construction of W; schemes.tex Tag 01IK, lemma-open-subspace-scheme.

proof.text: Fix $h:T\to B$, and write $r:A_T=A\times_BT\to A$ and $s:A_T\to T$. The square with upper arrow $r$, lower arrow $C_T=C\times_BT\to C$, and vertical arrows $f_T,f$ is Cartesian: giving a test map to $A\times_C C_T$ amounts to maps $a$ to $A$ and $t$ to $T$ with $pa=ht$, since its $C$-component must be $fa$. This is precisely the universal property of $A_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $f_T$ is a base change of $f$, is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], and [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change] gives $|U_{f_T}|=r^{-1}(|U_f|)$.

source.place: Tags 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type) and 0475 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified); schemes.tex Tag 01JP, fibre product universal property.

proof.text: A morphism is unramified exactly when its source is covered by unramified open restrictions: use the affine formulation in [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. If the restrictions cover, take their defining affine covers; their union is an affine cover with finite-type ring maps and zero relative differentials, which is that same definition globally. Consequently $f_T$ is unramified if and only if $U_{f_T}=A_T$, equivalently $r^{-1}(Z)=\varnothing$ by the preceding step.

source.place: Tag 02G4, definition-unramified, affine-cover definition; Tag 02GE, lemma-diagonal-unramified.

proof.text: We claim $s(r^{-1}(Z))=h^{-1}(p(Z))$. A point $z\in A_T$ with $r(z)\in Z$ satisfies $h(s(z))=p(r(z))$, giving one inclusion. Conversely let $t\in T$ and choose $a\in Z$ with $p(a)=h(t)=:b$. The ring $\kappa(a)\otimes_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(t)$ is a tensor product of two nonzero $\kappa(b)$-vector spaces, hence nonzero (tensor a basis vector of each), so it has a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ (a maximal ideal). By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], applied to $p:A\to B$ and $h:T\to B$, the quadruple $(a,t,b,\mathfrak p)$ corresponds to a point $z\in A_T$ with $r(z)=a$ and $s(z)=t$. Therefore $t=s(z)\in s(r^{-1}(Z))$, proving the other inclusion. Thus $r^{-1}(Z)=\varnothing$ if and only if $h^{-1}(p(Z))=\varnothing$, since a set is empty if and only if its image under a function is empty.

source.place: Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product; Tag 05X8, final paragraph, expanded point argument.

proof.text: The condition $h^{-1}(p(Z))=\varnothing$ says exactly that $h(|T|)\subseteq |B_0|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] this implies a unique factorization through $B_0\hookrightarrow B$. Conversely such a factorization has image in $B_0$, hence the same empty inverse image. Combining the preceding equivalences proves both directions of the required universal property.
